subject: Performance assurance & monthly remedy terms for FinWave
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinWave IT Director <it-director@finwave.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Request: performance assurances and monthly credit structure

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinWave is excited about Redwood's throughput and the batching improvements. Before we move the procurement forward, Legal and Procurement need clarity on two items in your standard SLA:

1) Uptime commitment: we need a firm proposal for a baseline availability percentage (FinWave prefers 99.95% if feasible) and how monthly credits are calculated when that threshold is not met.

2) Latency SLO: our product team is asking for a p95 inference latency target (we're aiming for 150ms for 512-token requests). If that can't be guaranteed across mixed deployment modes, we need an outline of how latency-related remedies would be handled.

We understand there are standard maintenance carve-outs; can you confirm typical maintenance windows and how those affect remedy calculations?

Would you be able to share a proposed SLA amendment and credit matrix we can review? Also happy to schedule 30 min to walk through.

Best,
Anita Shah
Head of Infrastructure
FinWave

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finwave.com>
Cc: FinWave IT Director <it-director@finwave.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance assurances and monthly credit structure

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear asks. I've attached our editable SLA template (SLA_Template_v1.2.pdf) and sketched two practical options so Procurement can pick the right level of assurance:

Option A (Standard):
- Availability: 99.9% monthly
- Monthly remedy: pro-rata credit equal to percentage shortfall applied to that month's invoice, capped at 30% of the monthly invoice
- Typical maintenance: weekly 1 hour window (regional, announced) + monthly patch window up to 3 hours

Option B (Enhanced):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly (applies when customer commits to a Dedicated GPU pool)
- Monthly remedy: tiered credits (shortfall bands 0.01–0.05% = 10% credit; 0.05–0.2% = 25% credit; >0.2% = 50% credit), capped at 50% of monthly invoice
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maint windows announced 48 hours in advance; emergency maintenance with post-facto notice for P1 fixes

Latency considerations: p95 150ms is achievable on Dedicated pools for the 512-token profile with the quantization and batching configuration we discussed. For mixed/hosted routing we can provide a regional p95 target and a fallback variance clause. I'll flag Ben from Ops to provide more detail on capacity/latency tradeoffs.

If this reads reasonable, I'll loop Legal for redlines and propose a short call Thursday to align.

Attachments: SLA_Template_v1.2.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance assurances and monthly credit structure

Marissa — forwarding my initial redlines for Anita's team to consider. I attached a doc (FinWave_SLA_redlines.docx) with tracked items but summarizing here: 

- Cap on monthly remedy: propose maximum aggregate remedy not to exceed 50% of monthly recurring charges (protects business viability).
- Carveouts: clarify scheduled maintenance (we propose standard weekly window + one monthly patch window) and add force majeure language consistent with enterprise contracts.
- Measurement: define measurement method (region-by-region telemetry from Redwood Console, using rolling 30-day windows) and an objective dispute-resolution process (30 days to present telemetry; if unresolved escalate to arbitration).
- Latency SLAs: suggest converting latency targets to a best-effort commitment with service credits only for availability breaches. Latency quantification is noisy across mixed routing; if customer wants hard latency SLAs, require Dedicated pool + isolation commitments.

Please send the redlines to Anita as a single consolidated draft. We'll keep the remedy math transparent but defensible.

On the DocuSign front, I'll prepare a short amendment once FinWave confirms which option they prefer.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-03T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance assurances and monthly credit structure

Looping in ops perspective. Technical notes for Anita and FinWave's SREs: 

- Dedicated pool vs hosted routing: Dedicated GPU pools with pinned capacity and reserved instances give us the isolation needed to guarantee p95 150ms for the 512-token profile. Hosted/shared capacity introduces variance due to noisy neighbors and autoscaling windows.
- Measurement windows: p95 measured at the Redwood gateway and aggregated per-region by request type. If FinWave routes cross regions, latency SLO should be regional (e.g., US-WEST p95 = X ms).
- Maintenance: we can agree to a baseline weekly maintenance of 1 hour (low-traffic window) and a monthly 3-hour patch window. Emergency maintenance will be tracked and notified; emergency P1s are excluded from remedy.
- Practical compromise: baseline availability 99.9% for hosted, 99.95% for Dedicated (as Marissa proposed). For latency, offer a dedicated-latency SLA tied to a minimum committed QPS and memory/KV cache configs.

I'll attach a small CSV with observed latency profiles by instance class to illustrate variance. Happy to join the alignment call.

Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure Operations
